audit.why: Packet win rate is 62.5 over 8 games. That is the smallest sample in the slice and I would not build an argument on it; the stored TRICKY 7/10 rating is a reasonable hedge and I left it alone.

audit.whatIsWrong: Cell Division's revive is never mentioned. The file only ever discusses the blobs as a sustain mechanic ('blob-pickup sustain', 'deny his passive blobs').
audit.why: On taking fatal damage Zac splits into four bloblets and reforms with health scaled to whichever survive, on a five-minute cooldown. Mel's entire payoff is a threshold execute — Golden Eclipse landing the kill is the plan. Against Cell Division that kill refunds itself unless the bloblets are cleared, and the player is left with no ultimate for the fight that follows. The site's own what-kills-me.js line for Zac says exactly this ('His blobs revive him — stomp them'); the matchup text never does.
audit.corrected: Stated the reform in winCon, phases[4].why, spikes[1].text, whys[4], content.mid, loading and report[1].t.

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.foe[2] says 'Q knockup into W slow' and content.early warns about being flung into 'his Q-W CC'.
audit.why: Zac's W is Unstable Matter — a 350-range burst of percent-max-health magic damage with no slow on it at all. The slows in his kit are on Stretching Strikes and Let's Bounce!. Mislabelling W as the slow sends the player looking for the wrong effect, and it hides the two things about Unstable Matter that actually matter to a squishy mage: it is only 350 range, and it is percent max health, so it does not care what she builds.
audit.corrected: Named Unstable Matter and its 350 range in wants.foe[2] and whys[3].
sources: champ-data/_kits/zac.json (W Unstable Matter, range 350, percentHealth; slow flag sits on Q and R)

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[0] and content.early both say 'Zac has no dash early, just slow walk speed', and wants.foe[2] frames Stretching Strikes as something he uses 'once he's actually on top of you'.
audit.why: Stretching Strikes is an 800-range grab. Mel's Radiant Volley is 950 and her auto 550, so his opening CC threatens from further out than she can attack — the lane is not the free walk-up punish the text describes. Elastic Slingshot is also available from level 1 or 2 if he takes it, so 'no dash early' is a level-dependent claim the file states unconditionally.
audit.corrected: Replaced both with the real 800 range on Stretching Strikes and reframed the early game around the root denying the launch.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing says that Zac pays health for his abilities.
audit.why: Stretching Strikes, Unstable Matter and Elastic Slingshot all cost a percentage of Zac's current health — he has no mana bar at all. For a champion whose whole win condition is a health-threshold execute, that is the single most exploitable fact in the matchup: every time he uses his kit to farm or trade he moves himself toward Mel's execute range for free. It appears nowhere.
audit.corrected: Added the health-cost lever to whys[0], spikes[2].text and content.early.
sources: champ-data/_kits/zac.json (resource None; Q, W and E all cost % of current Health)

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d, report[5].t and loading all tell the player to 'check it before every step-up' without a single number. tradeBad, dontsFull[2].d and breakdown.trading say Rebuttal is 'gone for twenty seconds'.
audit.why: Elastic Slingshot is 21/18/15/12/9 — a whiffed one at rank 1 hands Mel 21 seconds, which is two full Radiant Volley rotations. Stretching Strikes is 14/12.5/11/9.5/8 and Unstable Matter is a flat 5. Rebuttal is 38/35/33/29/26, so 38 at lane rank, not twenty. A matchup framed entirely around cooldown-watching contained no cooldowns.
audit.corrected: Put the real figures into breakdown.cooldowns, phases[3].why, dosFull, loading, report[5].t and whys[2], and corrected the Rebuttal number everywhere.

audit.whatIsWrong: Solar Snare's root is never connected to Elastic Slingshot beyond 'he can't dash out of the root'.
audit.why: Elastic Slingshot is a dash, and a rooted champion cannot cast one. That makes the root a pre-emptive denial of his entire engage rather than something to land after he arrives — which is how the rest of the file reads it ('root the landing'). It is also the only defensive tool in this matchup whose behaviour is verifiable.
audit.corrected: Made root-denies-launch explicit in spikes[0].text, whys[1], content.early, dosFull[0].d, breakdown.cooldowns and report[5].t.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[3].text, wants.you[0], whys[2] and content.early all instruct the player to 'delete the E projectile' / 'eat it with W's projectile wall' — i.e. to stop Elastic Slingshot with Rebuttal.
audit.why: I could not verify this and I did not edit around it. zac.json flags E as both 'projectile' and 'dash', which cannot both drive Rebuttal's behaviour, and the same ability also carries a 'grounding' flag that is plainly a keyword artefact of Riot's phrase 'attaches his arms to the ground' — Elastic Slingshot applies no Grounded. Elastic Slingshot launches Zac's own body, which reads as a self-displacement rather than something Rebuttal can reflect. If the flag is wrong, four separate strings are telling the player to spend her only defensive cooldown on an engage it does not stop.
audit.corrected: NOT EDITED — flagged for a Wiki check. I rewrote whys[2] to lean on the 21-second cooldown instead, which is true either way, and left spikes[3], wants.you[0] and the relevant clause of content.early untouched rather than assert a direction I cannot source.
sources: champ-data/_kits/zac.json (E flags: projectile, dash, grounding — grounding is demonstrably a false derivation)

audit.whatIsWrong: Itemization ends with 'Add anti-heal early into his sustain' and names no item.
audit.why: Zac's sustain is Cell Division's blob pickups, and the counter is an actual Grievous Wounds source. On an AP mage that is Morellonomicon. 'Add anti-heal' is a note-to-self, not a build instruction.
audit.corrected: Named Morellonomicon in report[8].t and content.mid.

notes: UNVERIFIED CLAIM I DELIBERATELY DID NOT TOUCH: four strings (spikes[3].text, wants.you[0], whys[2] as written, and one clause of content.early) tell the player to stop Elastic Slingshot with Rebuttal — 'delete the E projectile', 'eat it with W's projectile wall'. zac.json flags E as projectile AND dash AND grounding. The grounding flag is certainly a keyword artefact of Riot's phrase 'attaches his arms to the ground' — Elastic Slingshot applies no Grounded — which makes the projectile flag on the same ability suspect too, since the ability launches Zac's own body. I could not resolve it from the kit files and would not guess, so I left those strings alone and rewrote whys[2] around the 21-second cooldown, which is true either way. Please check the Wiki: if Rebuttal does not stop the sling, four strings are telling Mel to spend her only defensive cooldown on an engage that goes through it. SAME PATTERN, DIFFERENT ABILITY: zac.json also flags Q Stretching Strikes as a projectile. I made no claim about reflecting it. LEVEL CHART MISMATCH: content.win is [Mel,Mel,Mel,Mel,Mel,Mel,Skill] while full.phases sides are [Skill,Skill,Skill,Skill,Skill,Zac,Zac]. Milder than the other matchups in this slice but still two different charts for one matchup. I left the TRICKY 7/10 rating alone — 8 games is not enough sample to argue with it. WKM_LINES for zac are correct and actually contain the revive fact the matchup text was missing.
